titleZh: 逃出试点陷阱——任务级的快，掩盖不了设计级的漂移：麦肯锡的 agentic HR「北极星倒推法」
titleEn: Escaping the pilot trap: Building HR for the agentic era
author: Asmus Komm, Bryan Hancock, Sandra Durth
authorTitle: 麦肯锡合伙人（汉堡 / 华盛顿 / 科隆），People & Organizational Performance 业务线
summary: 人人一个下午就能搭 agent 的时代，「先小步试点」不再保守——必须先定 2030 北极星再倒推实施。
keyPoints: **试点陷阱 = 任务快、设计漂**：失控的局部实验会比中央团队编目更快地固化成碎片化 agent 景观——过去没蓝图浪费时间，现在浪费的是蓝图本身。
**北极星必须对三大张力表态**：编排平台归属（IT 排队 vs HR 影子栈）、个性化投入 vs 监控感（边界由员工信任划定）、自动化工作 vs 加速人的判断力与学徒路径。
**2030 图景：三层 Ulrich 模型合并为单层产品+平台组织**：约 2/3 HR 活动可全自动化或交付层自动化，战略时间 15%→50%，另有 20% 用于管 agent。
insight: 把 HR 换成任何职能都成立：agent 转型的分水岭不在技术而在治理——谁先定义人机运营模式的终局，谁才有资格谈快赢。

bilingual.en:
Organizations that create the most effective agentic HR functions don't just scale pilots. They define the human–agent operating model for the function first, then work backward to implementation.

Every HR leader we speak with now asks the same question about creating an agentic HR function: We understand the general destination, but how do we get there?
bilingual.zh:
打造出最有效 agentic HR 职能的组织，做的不只是把试点规模化。它们先定义整个职能的人机协作运营模式，再倒推回实施路径。

如今我们交流过的每一位 HR 负责人都在问同一个问题：建设 agentic HR 职能，大方向我们明白，但路怎么走？

bilingual.en: We believe their approach should be rooted in what makes the agentic transformation different. In earlier HR transformation waves, the human was always the unit of execution, and technology was a tool that humans operated. Agents change that assumption. They can reason, act across systems, and be orchestrated into teams that are supervised and held accountable. The rise of agents changes the redesign problem in two ways.
bilingual.zh: 我们认为，答案应扎根于 agentic 转型与以往的本质不同。在此前历次 HR 转型浪潮中，人始终是执行的基本单元，技术只是人操作的工具。Agent 改变了这一假设：它们能推理、能跨系统行动、能被编排成受监督、可问责的团队。Agent 的兴起从两个方面改变了重构问题本身。

bilingual.en: First, speed and frontline customization increase sharply. A payroll specialist or a recruiter can now configure a working agent in an afternoon using low-code tools. This is the greatest accelerant of the transformation and, at the same time, its greatest governance challenge. Local experimentation and design, without proper guardrails, can harden into a fragmented landscape of one-off agents faster than any central team can catalog it.
bilingual.zh: 第一，速度和一线自主定制能力急剧上升。一名薪酬专员或招聘官现在用低码工具一个下午就能配置出一个能用的 agent。这是转型最大的加速器，同时也是最大的治理挑战。缺乏恰当护栏的局部实验和设计，会以任何中央团队都来不及编目的速度，固化成一片碎片化的一次性 agent 景观。

bilingual.en: Second, HR must transform itself at the same pace it is asking the enterprise to move. In the ERP and agile eras, HR was largely a downstream adopter of changes designed elsewhere. In the agentic era, HR has a dual mandate as both the architect of the enterprise's human–agent redesign and a subject of that same redesign. A function that moves slower than the organization it advises, or that automates tasks while preaching workflow redesign, forfeits the credibility to lead.
bilingual.zh: 第二，HR 必须以它要求全企业转型的同等速度转型自己。在 ERP 和敏捷时代，HR 基本是别处设计好的变革的下游采纳者。而在 agentic 时代，HR 肩负双重使命：既是全企业人机协作重构的架构师，又是这场重构的对象本身。一个比自己所辅导的组织走得还慢的职能，或者一边宣讲工作流重构一边只做任务自动化的职能，将丧失领导变革的公信力。

bilingual.en:
The implication is uncomfortable for leaders trained on the last two decades of transformation: The instinct to "start small and learn" is no longer conservative. When any specialist can stand up an agent in an afternoon, starting small happens whether leadership sanctions it or not. The question is whether those efforts unfold within a deliberate design or instead of one.

In prior transformations, moving without a blueprint cost time. In this one, it costs the blueprint itself—every ungoverned agent hardens a fragment of the old operating model into code. We call this the pilot trap: speed at the level of the task, drift at the level of the design. That is why the redesign can't be managed pilot by pilot and why the journey must run from what we call "North Star back."
bilingual.zh:
这个推论对被过去二十年转型经验训练出来的领导者而言并不舒服：「先小步开始、边做边学」的直觉不再是保守稳妥的。当任何专员一个下午就能立起一个 agent，「小步开始」无论领导层批不批准都会发生。问题只在于：这些努力是在一个深思熟虑的设计之内展开，还是取而代之。

在以往的转型中，没有蓝图就行动，代价是时间。而这一次，代价是蓝图本身——每一个失控的 agent 都把旧运营模式的一块碎片固化进代码。我们称之为「试点陷阱」（pilot trap）：任务层面的快，设计层面的漂移。这就是为什么这场重构不能一个试点一个试点地管理，为什么整个旅程必须按我们所说的「北极星倒推」（North Star back）来走。

bilingual.en:
A North Star should solve three core tensions

The default should be the North Star–back approach: Define the 2030 human–agent operating model for the function first, then work backward to the implementation sequence, capability investments, governance structures, and quick wins needed to get there. Everything else is an entry point into that journey, not a substitute for it.

In creating the North Star, some elements are commonly understood: AI frees humans for more strategic work, and humans bring judgment while agents propel scale. The harder conversations we have with executives involve three core tensions.
bilingual.zh:
## 北极星必须解决三大核心张力

默认路径应该是北极星倒推法：先定义该职能 2030 年的人机协作运营模式，再倒推出实施顺序、能力投资、治理结构和到达终点所需的快赢。其他一切都只是进入这段旅程的切入点，而不是它的替代品。

在制定北极星时，有些要素已是共识：AI 把人解放出来做更具战略性的工作，人提供判断力，agent 提供规模。而我们与高管们更难展开的对话，围绕三大核心张力。

bilingual.en: Who owns the orchestration platform? The agents belong to HR, but the platform they run on is enterprise infrastructure covering identity, security, integration, and orchestration. If IT owns it outright, HR waits in a queue and loses the pace advantage that makes agents valuable. If HR builds its own, the enterprise inherits a shadow stack. The same question repeats inside HR: Which agents are built centrally as products, and which are configured locally by the people who own the workflow?
bilingual.zh: **谁拥有编排平台？** agent 属于 HR，但它们运行的平台是企业级基础设施，涵盖身份、安全、集成与编排。如果 IT 完全拥有平台，HR 就得排队等待，失去让 agent 有价值的速度优势；如果 HR 自建，企业就继承了一套影子技术栈。同样的问题在 HR 内部还会重复出现：哪些 agent 由中央作为产品来建，哪些由拥有工作流的一线人员本地配置？

bilingual.en: Investment versus surveillance: Agentic HR can finally tailor its work to the individual rather than the segment, anticipating a career move, curating the next role, and tailoring development to how someone actually works. The same capability that goes one notch too far or is introduced without transparency stops feeling like an investment and starts feeling like surveillance. The line is not set by regulation. It is set by whether employees believe the personalization serves them.
bilingual.zh: **投入感 vs 监控感**：agentic HR 终于可以把工作从「面向人群分层」做到「面向个体定制」——预判职业异动、策划下一个岗位、按每个人的实际工作方式定制发展路径。但同样的能力，只要越界一格，或在缺乏透明度的情况下引入，就会从「组织对我的投入」变成「组织对我的监控」。这条线不是由法规划定的，而是由员工是否相信这种个性化在为他们服务来划定的。

bilingual.en:
Automating work versus accelerating people: The easy decision is what agents should absorb. The harder one is determining which human capabilities become more valuable (judgment, relationships, coaching, persuasion) and where the organization will deliberately accelerate them, in HR and the business alike. That includes cognitive load, or the amount of mental effort employees must expend as they incorporate AI into their work, as well as rebuilding the apprenticeship path. If agents take the entry-level work, the next generation's judgment has to be developed on purpose rather than absorbed on the job.

None of these tensions is solved once; they are managed continuously. A North Star that does not take an explicit position on all three is not yet a North Star.
bilingual.zh:
**自动化工作 vs 加速人的成长**：容易的决策是 agent 该吸收哪些工作；难的是判断哪些人类能力会变得更值钱（判断力、关系、教练能力、说服力），以及组织将在哪里刻意加速这些能力——HR 和业务侧都是如此。这包括认知负荷（员工把 AI 融入工作所需付出的心智努力），也包括重建学徒成长路径：如果 agent 拿走了入门级工作，下一代人的判断力就必须被有意识地培养，而不能再指望在岗位上自然习得。

这三大张力没有一次性解法，只能持续管理。一个没有对这三者明确表态的北极星，还不算北极星。

bilingual.en:
Three entry points, not three strategies

Where, then, should an organization generate its first proof points? Bottom-up use cases, end-to-end process redesign, and domain-by-domain reinvention are best understood as entry points into the North Star–backed journey. Deciding which to tackle first depends on an organization's starting point, data maturity, risk appetite, and leadership readiness.
bilingual.zh:
## 三个切入点，而不是三种战略

那么，组织的第一批证明点应该从哪里产生？自下而上的用例、端到端流程重构、按域重塑，这三者最好被理解为进入「北极星护航之旅」的三个切入点。先做哪个，取决于组织的起点、数据成熟度、风险偏好和领导层的就绪程度。

bilingual.en:
Bottom-up use cases: Some organizations start by identifying pain points across the HR function, agentifying them selectively, and building momentum through quick wins. One organization following this path implemented 50 use cases, each valuable on a small scale, from an AI-powered chatbot for employee queries to automated meeting synthesis to AI-augmented learning and performance management. As a result, the company identified significant annual cost savings along with meaningful improvements in HR service levels.

The danger of this approach is that its impact can be limited if individual use cases aren't tied to a broader redesign of workflows, roles, and HR capabilities. In some cases, organizations improve the efficiency of processes that, once work is redesigned end to end, are ultimately eliminated or absorbed into entirely different workflows. This is the pilot trap at work: effort spent perfecting steps that the future operating model eliminates.
bilingual.zh:
**自下而上的用例**：一些组织从识别 HR 职能各处的痛点开始，有选择地将其 agent 化，通过快赢积累势能。一家走这条路的企业落地了 50 个用例，每个在小尺度上都有价值——从员工问询的 AI 聊天机器人、自动会议纪要，到 AI 增强的学习与绩效管理。最终该公司识别出可观的年度成本节约，同时 HR 服务水平显著改善。

这条路的危险在于：如果单个用例不与更大范围的工作流、角色和 HR 能力重构挂钩，其影响可能很有限。有些组织努力提升某些流程的效率，而这些流程在端到端重构之后最终会被消灭，或被吸收进完全不同的工作流。这就是试点陷阱的现场版：把力气花在完善那些未来运营模式会直接删掉的步骤上。

bilingual.en:
End-to-end process redesign: Other organizations focus on a small number of end-to-end HR processes, reimagining them as human-plus-agent systems and using them as a blueprint for broader change. In practice, the starting point is often a set of administrative processes such as payroll, document management, onboarding administration, or query handling. These workflows typically offer cleaner data, more transparent process steps, and faster time to value. A global auto manufacturer followed this path by redesigning two end-to-end processes in parallel. Based on what it learned, the manufacturer developed a comprehensive vision for a full redesign of its HR function.

Domain-by-domain reinvention: The most ambitious organizations take each HR domain (talent acquisition, learning and development, total rewards, performance management, HR business partnering) and rebuild it from the ground up as an agentic system. This is not incremental improvement but a reinvention of how each domain operates, is staffed, and creates value. In practice, this is the North Star–back journey begun at full scale, the entry point for organizations whose conviction and readiness allow them to skip the on-ramp.
bilingual.zh:
**端到端流程重构**：另一些组织聚焦少数几条端到端 HR 流程，把它们重新构想为「人+agent」系统，并以此作为更大变革的蓝图。实践中，起点通常是一组行政类流程——薪酬发放、文档管理、入职行政、问询处理。这类工作流通常数据更干净、流程步骤更透明、见效更快。一家全球汽车制造商走了这条路，并行重构两条端到端流程，并基于所学制定了 HR 职能全面重构的完整愿景。

**按域重塑**：最有雄心的组织把每个 HR 域（招聘、学习与发展、整体薪酬、绩效管理、HRBP）从地基开始重建为 agentic 系统。这不是渐进改良，而是对每个域如何运转、如何配员、如何创造价值的重塑。实际上，这就是从全尺度直接开始的北极星倒推之旅——是那些信念和就绪度允许它们跳过匝道的组织的切入点。

bilingual.en: The prescription is straightforward. Every organization needs early proof points, and they can legitimately come from any of these entry points. What cannot vary is the governing logic: Proof points must be selected, sequenced, and judged against a clear view of the future operating model. The journey must be deliberate, sequenced, and governed, rather than emerging organically from a collection of disconnected pilots.
bilingual.zh: 处方很直接：每个组织都需要早期证明点，它们可以合理地来自上述任何一个切入点。但不能变的是治理逻辑：证明点的选择、排序和评判，必须对照一幅清晰的未来运营模式图景。这段旅程必须是深思熟虑的、有序的、被治理的，而不是从一堆互不相连的试点中自发长出来的。

bilingual.en:
The destination: What HR could look like by 2030

For organizations that have begun their agentic journey, a clearer picture of the future HR function is emerging. McKinsey analysis indicates that, by 2030, roughly two-thirds of today's HR activities, from requisition management and candidate screening to payroll processing, onboarding, and benefits administration, could be fully automated or fully automated in delivery (Exhibit 1).

![Exhibit 1](/reads/mckinsey-agentic-hr-pilot-trap/exhibit-1.svg)
*Exhibit 1 · 麦肯锡分析：到 2030 年，约 2/3 的现有 HR 活动可实现全自动化或交付层全自动化。*
bilingual.zh:
## 终点：2030 年的 HR 会是什么样

对已经启程的组织而言，未来 HR 职能的图景正变得清晰。麦肯锡分析显示：到 2030 年，当前 HR 活动的约三分之二——从招聘需求管理、候选人筛选，到薪酬处理、入职、福利管理——可以实现全自动化（fully automated）或交付层全自动化（fully automated in delivery）（见 Exhibit 1）。

bilingual.en:
Fully automated means an agent completes the work end to end with no routine human involvement, such as generating an employment verification letter, scheduling an interview loop, or answering a benefits eligibility question. Fully automated in delivery means agents execute the workflow while humans retain ownership of policy, outcomes, and exceptions. Payroll is the canonical case: Agents run the cycle, and humans design the policy and adjudicate the garnishment, the cross-border complication, and the case that doesn't fit the rules. Augmented describes the remaining work, in which humans lead and agents prepare, analyze, and draft.

The distinction matters because the larger share of HR work falls into the second and third categories. That is exactly why a task-automation framing understates the redesign requirement. The question across HR is not whether a human is involved, but where human judgment sits in a workflow that agents largely execute.
bilingual.zh:
**全自动化**指 agent 端到端完成工作、无常规人工参与，例如生成在职证明、安排面试环节、回答福利资格问题。**交付层全自动化**指 agent 执行工作流，但人保留对政策、结果和例外的所有权。薪酬是典型案例：agent 跑周期，人设计政策，并裁决工资扣押、跨境复杂情形和规则覆盖不了的个案。**增强（augmented）**则描述其余工作——人主导，agent 负责准备、分析和起草。

这个区分很重要，因为 HR 工作的大头落在第二、第三类。这正是「任务自动化」框架低估重构需求的原因：贯穿 HR 的问题不是「有没有人参与」，而是在一个大部分由 agent 执行的工作流里，人的判断力放在哪个位置。

bilingual.en:
The implications for how HR professionals spend their working day are profound. Today, the typical HR function allocates roughly 40 percent of its time to operational delivery, 30 percent to program and project execution, and 15 percent to ad hoc problem solving. That leaves roughly 15 percent for strategic engagement and innovation. In an agentic HR model, that balance is likely to shift dramatically: operational delivery shrinks to approximately 5 percent of human time, program and project execution to roughly 10 percent, and ad hoc problem solving to 15 percent. This allows 50 percent of human time to be dedicated to strategic engagement and innovation, while roughly 20 percent is allotted to agentic capability management (Exhibit 2).

![Exhibit 2](/reads/mckinsey-agentic-hr-pilot-trap/exhibit-2.svg)
*Exhibit 2 · 时间分配迁移：运营交付 40%→5%，项目执行 30%→10%，临时问题 15%→15%，战略参与与创新 15%→50%，新增约 20% 用于 agent 能力管理。*
bilingual.zh: 这对 HR 从业者如何度过工作日影响深远。今天，典型 HR 职能约 40% 的时间花在运营交付、30% 在项目执行、15% 在临时问题处理，只剩约 15% 用于战略参与和创新。在 agentic HR 模式下，这个比例可能剧变：运营交付缩到约 5%，项目执行约 10%，临时问题处理 15%——从而释放 50% 的人类时间投入战略参与和创新，另有约 20% 分配给 agent 能力管理（见 Exhibit 2）。

bilingual.en: That last category deserves more attention than it usually gets. In the destination model, a meaningful share of HR jobs will consist of owning agents. The roughly 20 percent of human time devoted to agentic capability management is not a rounding category. It is HR professionals configuring agents in low-code environments, writing and reviewing the logic that those agents follow, testing their work before release, monitoring their performance and drift, and retiring them when the workflow changes. Work that sits closer to coding and product management than to case handling will become a normal HR career rather than a specialist sideline, and organizations should plan their hiring, training, and career paths accordingly.
bilingual.zh: 最后这个类别值得比通常更多的关注。在终局模型中，相当一部分 HR 岗位的内容将是「拥有 agent」。这约 20% 的人类时间不是四舍五入的凑数项，而是 HR 专业人员在低码环境里配置 agent、编写和评审 agent 遵循的逻辑、发布前测试其工作、监控其性能与漂移、并在工作流变化时让其退役。这类更接近编程和产品管理而非个案处理的工作，将成为 HR 的常规职业路径而非专家副业——组织应据此规划招聘、培训和职业通道。

bilingual.en: The agentic model does not eliminate HR domains. Rather, it rewires them for purposeful collaboration between human judgment and agentic execution. Take talent acquisition: Agents clean records and analyze who the right candidate might be. A separate agent scores candidates and undertakes ranking and sourcing. Another contacts candidates and schedules interviews. A coordinating agent sits atop the overall process, interacting with the underlying agents. The recruiter's job becomes designing, supervising, and improving that system, and owning the moments where judgment, relationship, and persuasion decide the outcome.
bilingual.zh: agentic 模式并不消灭 HR 各域，而是把它们重新接线，实现人类判断与 agent 执行的目的性协作。以招聘为例：一个 agent 清洗记录并分析谁可能是合适的候选人；另一个 agent 给候选人打分、排序和寻源；再一个联系候选人、安排面试；一个协调 agent 坐在整个流程顶端，与底层 agent 交互。招聘官的工作变成设计、监督和改进这个系统，并把握那些由判断力、关系和说服力决定结果的关键时刻。

bilingual.en:
The structure of the function changes as well. The HR function can streamline its operating model by moving away from the traditional three-tiered Ulrich model, with HR split into business partnering, shared-services centers, and centers of excellence (COEs). In the new model, these tiers merge into one layer as shared-services centers become largely digitized and agentified, while COEs retain a few deep experts organized into tribes. These moves create a centrally steered, flexibly resourced network that becomes more strategic, collaborative, fluid, and data driven.

What does this look like on an actual organizational chart? One credible answer appears in Exhibit 3, and three ideas define it.

![Exhibit 3](/reads/mckinsey-agentic-hr-pilot-trap/exhibit-3.svg)
*Exhibit 3 · 2030 年 agentic HR 的组织架构图：产品与平台型组织，两个战略组 + 两个产品组 + 一个平台组。*
bilingual.zh:
职能的结构也随之改变。HR 可以摆脱传统的三层 Ulrich 模型（业务伙伴 BP、共享服务中心 SSC、专家中心 COE），精简其运营模式。在新模型中，随着共享服务中心大幅数字化和 agent 化，三层合并为一层，COE 保留少数深度专家、按部落（tribe）组织。这些变化造就一个中央统筹、资源灵活调配的网络——更战略、更协作、更流动、更数据驱动。

落到真实的组织架构图上是什么样？Exhibit 3 给出一个可信的答案，由三个理念定义。

bilingual.en:
The first is the model itself. HR runs as a product and platform organization rather than a set of functional pillars. Work is organized around the products that the function ships and the platform they run on, so end-to-end redesign is native to the structure instead of negotiated across silos, and agent performance is owned the way any product feature is owned.

The second is that strategy work is concentrated in two groups. An enterprise workforce architecture group runs workforce simulations and the skills graph, and redesigns jobs and workflows across the business units, which is what makes the chief human resources officer (CHRO) a genuine peer to the chief information officer (CIO) on agent strategy rather than a customer of it. Alongside it, the traditional business partner population is revamped into small workforce pods, one per business unit, each a senior strategist with one or two analysts, focused on the hardest people calls in the business rather than on program delivery.
bilingual.zh:
第一是模型本身：HR 作为「产品与平台组织」运行，而不是一组职能支柱。工作围绕该职能交付的产品及其运行平台来组织，端到端重构因此是结构原生的，而不是跨竖井谈判出来的；agent 的性能像任何产品功能一样被明确拥有。

第二是战略工作集中到两个组。企业劳动力架构组负责劳动力模拟和技能图谱，并跨业务单元重新设计岗位与工作流——正是这一点让 CHRO 在 agent 战略上成为 CIO 真正的对等伙伴，而不是它的客户。与之并列，传统 BP 群体改组为小型劳动力 pod，每个业务单元一个，由一名资深战略家带一两名分析师，聚焦业务中最难的人事决策而非项目交付。

bilingual.en:
The third is that everything else consolidates into two product groups and one platform group. The talent products platform bundles hiring, growth, mobility, and performance under product managers who own their funnels end to end, including the performance of the agents running them. Employee experience products include rewards, recognition, and listening, with culture and change work on trust and belonging explicitly reserved for human employees. Beneath both sits a single people platform and intelligence organization that runs the agents, the data, and the service layer, with humans catching the exceptions.

This is the org chart version of the merged, single-layer model described above, and its demands are as clear as its logic. It requires product management muscle that most HR functions do not have today, a data foundation strong enough to run a skills graph, and a CHRO with a real enterprise workforce design mandate. Fewer organizations can start here. But for a function defining its North Star, this is what the destination looks like drawn as boxes and lines.
bilingual.zh:
第三是其余一切整合为两个产品组加一个平台组。人才产品平台把招聘、成长、流动、绩效捆绑在产品经理名下，产品经理端到端拥有自己的漏斗——包括跑在其中的 agent 的性能。员工体验产品涵盖薪酬激励、认可和倾听，其中关于信任与归属感的文化与变革工作被明确保留给人类员工。两者之下是单一的「人员平台与智能」组织，运营 agent、数据和服务层，人负责接住例外。

这就是前述「合并单层模型」的组织架构图版本，其要求和逻辑一样清晰：需要大多数 HR 职能今天还不具备的产品管理肌肉、强到能跑技能图谱的数据地基，以及真正握有企业劳动力设计授权的 CHRO。能从这里起步的组织不多。但对一个正在定义北极星的职能而言，这就是把终点画成方框和连线的样子。

bilingual.en:
Human capabilities in the agentic HR model

The shift away from centers of excellence, HR business partners, and shared services toward a centrally steered, flexibly resourced network creates multiple new roles. Four of the most common include:

People strategist: Sets direction, translates business strategy into people priorities, and ensures that the right mix of human and agent capacity is deployed where it matters most. People technologist: Designs and maintains the agentic operating backbone, translating business needs into digital capabilities. Capability builders configure agentic workflows using low-code tools; agent integrators oversee governance, performance, and interoperability of agentic systems.
bilingual.zh:
## agentic HR 模式中的人类能力

从 COE、HRBP、共享服务转向中央统筹、灵活配置的网络，会催生多个新角色。最常见的四个包括：

**People strategist（人才战略家）**：定方向，把业务战略翻译成人才优先级，确保人与 agent 的产能组合部署在最关键处。**People technologist（人才技术专家）**：设计并维护 agentic 运营骨干，把业务需求翻译成数字能力——其中能力构建者用低码工具配置 agentic 工作流，agent 集成者负责 agentic 系统的治理、性能与互操作性。

bilingual.en:
People scientist: Provides the ethical, legal, and evidence-based guardrails for the agentic enterprise. This role oversees bias, risk, and data integrity in agentic workflows; runs experiments and validations to ensure outcomes are ethical and effective; and handles complex employee escalations requiring human judgment. This goes beyond system-level documentation. Under regulations such as the EU AI Act, each individual agentic decision must be explainable and contestable at the case level, not just the system as a whole.

Flow-to-work generalist: A flexible, high-skill talent pool deployed dynamically across HR to deliver strategic projects, fill capability gaps, or provide nuanced human engagement where automation cannot. This archetype also serves as an apprenticeship path toward future strategist or technologist roles.

Other new profiles are emerging as well, including agent orchestrators who design and supervise agent workflows, hybrid managers who lead blended human–agent teams, and AI coaches who help employees integrate AI into daily work. At the same time, other roles will disappear—for example, interpretive roles that historically were required to "connect the dots" across silos.
bilingual.zh:
**People scientist（人才科学家）**：为 agentic 企业提供伦理、法律和循证护栏。该角色监督 agentic 工作流中的偏见、风险与数据完整性；运行实验和验证以确保结果合乎伦理且有效；并处理需要人类判断的复杂员工升级事项。这超出了系统级文档的范畴——在欧盟 AI 法案等法规下，每一个 agentic 决策都必须在个案层面可解释、可申诉，而不只是系统整体。

**Flow-to-work generalist（流动型通才）**：一支灵活的高技能人才池，跨 HR 动态部署，交付战略项目、填补能力缺口，或在自动化做不到的地方提供有温度的人际互动。这一原型同时是通往未来战略家或技术专家角色的学徒路径。

其他新角色也在涌现：设计和监督 agent 工作流的 agent 编排者、领导人机混合团队的混合型经理、帮员工把 AI 融入日常工作的 AI 教练。与此同时，另一些角色将消失——例如那些历史上专为跨竖井「串联信息」而存在的解释性角色。

bilingual.en:
Four transition layers for agentic HR

While organizations are pursuing different paths toward an agentic HR function, the underlying transformation challenges are remarkably consistent. Achieving that transformation requires deliberate work across four interconnected areas. None can be addressed in isolation, and each must advance through a sequence of diagnosis, design, build, and pilot.

Workflows: Every HR process can be examined through the lens of what humans and agents can contribute, and redesigned accordingly. This layer is where the unit-of-analysis shift becomes operational: the deliverable is a redesigned workflow, not a list of automatable tasks.

Organization and talent: The structural shift requires assessing the current HR structure, full-time-employee mix, and skill distribution. Increasingly, those transition paths lead toward agent ownership: The people who once ran a process become the people who build, tune, and govern the agents that run it.
bilingual.zh:
## agentic HR 的四个转型层

尽管各组织通往 agentic HR 的路径不同，底层的转型挑战却出奇一致。实现转型需要在四个相互关联的领域做刻意的工作，任何一个都不能孤立处理，且每个都要走「诊断→设计→构建→试点」的序列。

**工作流**：每条 HR 流程都可以用「人和 agent 各能贡献什么」的透镜来检视并相应重构。这一层是「分析单元切换」落地的地方：交付物是一条重构后的工作流，而不是一份可自动化任务清单。

**组织与人才**：结构性转变要求评估当前 HR 架构、编制组合和技能分布。转型路径越来越多地通向 agent 所有权：曾经运行某个流程的人，成为构建、调优和治理运行该流程的 agent 的人。

bilingual.en:
Technology and data enablement: The agentic HR model runs on a unified foundation of technology and data. Building it starts with auditing the current tech stack, integrations, and data quality. From there, teams define the target architecture and build-versus-buy strategy, build core infrastructure such as integrations, APIs, and data pipelines, and validate system readiness, data integrity, and security before going live.

Transformation governance and change management: This is where most transformations succeed or fail. Success requires a transformation narrative and guiding principles, a transformation office with a clear governance cadence, AI-fluency programs, readiness assessments, and active change champions.
bilingual.zh:
**技术与数据使能**：agentic HR 模式运行在统一的技术与数据地基之上。建设从审计当前技术栈、集成和数据质量开始，继而定义目标架构和自建 vs 采购策略，构建集成、API、数据管道等核心基础设施，并在上线前验证系统就绪度、数据完整性和安全性。

**转型治理与变革管理**：这是大多数转型成败的分水岭。成功需要一套转型叙事和指导原则、一个有清晰治理节奏的转型办公室、AI 素养项目、就绪度评估，以及活跃的变革推动者。

bilingual.en:
Five decisions CHROs need to make now

The CHRO can begin HR's agentic journey by making five decisions, each of which shapes every subsequent move:

1. What is our North Star? What unique value should the people function deliver to the business in 2030, and what mix of humans and agents will deliver it? What will we stop doing entirely? Does our picture take a real position on the three core tensions, or does it duck them? This is a CHRO-level decision, with input from the CEO, CFO, and CIO.

2. Where do we enter, and in what sequence? Which entry point fits the organization's starting point: individual use cases, end-to-end processes, or full domains?

3. How do we rebuild HR's own capabilities? Which capability moves are no-regrets and should start now, from AI fluency and workflow-redesign skills to data foundations and a first cohort of agent owners?
bilingual.zh:
## CHRO 现在就要做的五个决定

CHRO 可以通过五个决定开启 HR 的 agentic 之旅，每一个都塑造后续所有动作：

**1. 我们的北极星是什么？** 2030 年人才职能应该向业务交付什么独特价值？由怎样的人机组合来交付？我们将彻底停止做哪些事？我们的图景是对三大核心张力真正表了态，还是回避了它们？这是 CHRO 级别的决定，需要 CEO、CFO、CIO 的输入。

**2. 从哪里切入、按什么顺序？** 哪个切入点适合组织的起点：单个用例、端到端流程，还是整域重塑？

**3. 如何重建 HR 自己的能力？** 哪些能力建设是无悔投入、现在就该启动——从 AI 素养和工作流重构技能，到数据地基和第一批 agent 所有者？

bilingual.en:
4. Who governs, and how do we balance frontline speed with enterprise coherence? Who leads the effort, and who holds decision rights when a local experiment conflicts with the enterprise architecture? Where does the orchestration platform sit: with IT, HR, or shared?

5. What is the value case, and which choices are reversible? What is the value at stake across efficiency, effectiveness, and experience, and how will progress be tracked against it? Just as important: Which early choices are foundational, which compound over time, and which can be safely undone? Knowing the difference is what keeps speed from becoming recklessness.

Answering these with rigor and honesty is how the agentic journey begins. Organizations that do this up-front work move faster, make fewer costly course corrections, and build the organizational alignment that sustains momentum through the inevitable challenges of a multiyear transformation.
bilingual.zh:
**4. 谁来治理？如何平衡一线速度与企业一致性？** 谁牵头？当局部实验与企业架构冲突时，决策权在谁手里？编排平台放在哪：IT、HR，还是共享？

**5. 价值账怎么算？哪些选择可逆？** 在效率、效果、体验三个维度上有多大价值在博弈？进展如何对照追踪？同样重要的是：哪些早期选择是地基性的、哪些会随时间复利、哪些可以安全撤销？分清这三者，才能让速度不变成鲁莽。

以严谨和诚实回答这五个问题，agentic 之旅才算真正开始。做足这些前置功课的组织走得更快、付出的纠偏代价更少，并能建立起支撑多年转型穿越必然挑战的组织共识。

bilingual.en: The journey to an agentic HR function is demanding. It requires courage, clarity, commitment, curiosity, and a willingness to make bold choices about what HR is for and how it should work. It is also one of the most significant opportunities available to HR leaders to build a function that is genuinely fit for the future, and to help the entire organization navigate into a new era of human–agent collaboration.
bilingual.zh: 通往 agentic HR 职能的旅程要求很高：需要勇气、清晰、承诺、好奇心，以及对「HR 为何存在、该如何运转」做出大胆抉择的意愿。但它也是 HR 领导者手中最重要的机会之一——建设一个真正面向未来的职能，并帮助整个组织驶入人机协作的新纪元。

quotes.en: In prior transformations, moving without a blueprint cost time. In this one, it costs the blueprint itself—every ungoverned agent hardens a fragment of the old operating model into code.
quotes.zh: 在以往的转型中，没有蓝图就行动，代价是时间。而这一次，代价是蓝图本身——每一个失控的 agent 都把旧运营模式的一块碎片固化进代码。

quotes.en: We call this the pilot trap: speed at the level of the task, drift at the level of the design.
quotes.zh: 我们称之为试点陷阱：任务层面的快，设计层面的漂移。

quotes.en: The instinct to "start small and learn" is no longer conservative. When any specialist can stand up an agent in an afternoon, starting small happens whether leadership sanctions it or not.
quotes.zh: 「先小步开始、边做边学」的直觉不再是保守稳妥的。当任何专员一个下午就能立起一个 agent，「小步开始」无论领导层批不批准都会发生。

quotes.en: The line is not set by regulation. It is set by whether employees believe the personalization serves them.
quotes.zh: 这条线不是由法规划定的，而是由员工是否相信这种个性化在为他们服务来划定的。

quotes.en: If agents take the entry-level work, the next generation's judgment has to be developed on purpose rather than absorbed on the job.
quotes.zh: 如果 agent 拿走了入门级工作，下一代人的判断力就必须被有意识地培养，而不能再指望在岗位上自然习得。

quotes.en: The question across HR is not whether a human is involved, but where human judgment sits in a workflow that agents largely execute.
quotes.zh: 贯穿 HR 的问题不是「有没有人参与」，而是在一个大部分由 agent 执行的工作流里，人的判断力放在哪个位置。

quotes.en: The people who once ran a process become the people who build, tune, and govern the agents that run it.
quotes.zh: 曾经运行某个流程的人，成为构建、调优和治理运行该流程的 agent 的人。

quotes.en: A North Star that does not take an explicit position on all three is not yet a North Star.
quotes.zh: 一个没有对这三大张力明确表态的北极星，还不算北极星。

secondaryReads.source: 麦肯锡《Is that AI agent worth it? Agentic economics and the modern operating model》
secondaryReads.pov: 同系列姊妹篇，从经济账角度补齐本文的组织视角：agent 的单位经济学（token 成本、监督成本、返工成本）如何决定哪些流程值得 agent 化——先算账再重构，与「北极星倒推」互为表里。
工程域的同构方案：麦肯锡讲 HR 怎么逃出试点陷阱，Anthropic 讲软件开发怎么逃——两者共享同一内核（先定终局运营模式、artifact 链治理、人的判断上移到 gate），可对照验证「北极星倒推」不是咨询话术而是跨职能的通用模式。

secondaryReads.source: 麦肯锡《Building expertise in the age of AI: Who trains the next generation?》
secondaryReads.pov: 展开本文「学徒路径断裂」这条暗线：agent 吃掉入门级工作后，判断力的代际传承机制必须被刻意重建——这是三大张力中「自动化 vs 加速人」最被低估的一半。
